title: Only One Building in China Has 10 Roof Beasts | China Travel Expert
description:
Look up at a Chinese palace roof and count the little animals marching down the corner ridge. They aren't just decoration - they're a rank system.

These ridge figures (跑兽 / 脊兽) are led by an immortal riding a bird, and behind him comes a line of guardian beasts. The rule is simple: the more beasts, the higher the building's status. Ordinary important halls get 3, 5, 7 or 9.

Only one building is allowed the full set of 10 - the Hall of Supreme Harmony (Taihedian) in the Forbidden City, the throne hall of the Ming and Qing emperors. The 10th figure, hangshi (行仈), a winged guardian, appears on no other roof in China.

🧭 Expert Tip: next time you're at the Forbidden City, stand below the Hall of Supreme Harmony and count the corner-ridge figures - it's the one place you can reach 10. Every other hall will stop short, and now you'll know why.

中国官殿屋顶角脊上的小兽数量标记等级：兽越多等级越高，多数殿宇是 3、5、7 个；只有故宫太和殿有全部 10 个，第 10 个“行仈”为太和殿所独有。
